title: A * in a policy variable's value or default
question: Does a * that a policy variable fills in act as a wildcard? AWS doesn't say. The analyzer refuses.

cases.name: star_in_a_value
cases.description: The caller's team tag is b*. IAM's tag rules don't allow a * in a tag value, but the simulator takes any value.

cases.name: star_in_a_default
cases.description: The default is class-of-*, and the caller has no team tag.

readings.IMPLICIT_DENY: it is a literal *, or the simulator's handling of a key left out of the call (see calibration)

cases.name: condition_star_in_a_value
cases.description: Third follow-up: star_in_a_value's question in a condition value. StringLike s3:prefix ${aws:PrincipalTag/team}/, for a caller whose team tag is b*, listing blue/.

readings.ALLOW: the * acts as a wildcard in a condition value
readings.IMPLICIT_DENY: it is a literal *, as in Resource

cases.name: condition_star_in_a_default
cases.description: Third follow-up: star_in_a_default's question in a condition value. StringLike s3:prefix ${aws:PrincipalTag/team, 'class-of-*'}/, for a caller with no team tag, listing class-of-2026/.

readings.ALLOW: the * acts as a wildcard in a condition value
readings.IMPLICIT_DENY: it is a literal *, as in Resource, or the simulator's handling of a key left out of the call (see calibration)
